scope: The full fraction-field paired determinant identity, using the preceding odd theorem and the actual subgroup hypothesis [G,G] subset H. No Lean build, integral denominator bound or finite auxiliary choice is claimed.

prerequisite.role: The previously reviewed odd theorem supplies the polarized odd primitives. The present review assumes that theorem and independently verifies the even completion.

audit_groups.details: Expansion of C(g)=chi(g)sum[kappa_i(g),Ad(rho(g))Y_i] gives the original inhomogeneous defect with positive sign. Subtraction leaves an even chi-twisted cocycle. The original conjugate-transpose relation and sY_i^T=Y_i give C(sigma g)=sC(g)^T.

audit_groups.topic: Trace correction on the exact subgroup
audit_groups.details: For arbitrary g, tr((C+sum lambda_i kappa_i)rho)=(chi(g)-1)sum tr(Y_i kappa_i rho). It vanishes on H, where chi is trivial. The proof does not assert vanishing outside H and keeps the original order lambda_i kappa_i.

audit_groups.topic: Group-algebra descent through the trace pairing
audit_groups.details: D(h)=psi(h)rho(h) is a derivation relative to pi:F[H]->E and has zero trace. For x in ker pi, tr(D(x)pi(y))=0 for every y. The span hypothesis and the matrix-unit trace pairing on E force D(x)=0 in every characteristic, including when the characteristic divides a block size.

With one base index in every nonempty block, S=sum delta(E_i,beta(i))E_beta(i),i satisfies delta(X)=SX-XS. The product-rule computation sums all diagonal units to the identity and requires no division by the dimension. The cocycle primitive has sign -S. Empty second blocks cause no problem.

After subtracting d_chi(-S), the residual vanishes on H. Normality and the cocycle identity put its values in the centralizer of rho(H), hence the center of E. The actual condition [G,G] subset H makes z(cg)=z(gc). Dividing by the specified nonzero chi(c)-1 then gives the global even primitive.

The global polarization identity implies d_chi(X^T)=s psi. Therefore (X+sX^T)/2 is an even primitive with sY_0^T=Y_0. Only the field being of characteristic different from two is needed for this division; no characteristic-zero rigidity is used.

The affine group over F5 with H trivial, rho=1, chi(a,b)=a and z(a,b)=b satisfies the weaker normal-subgroup and span/polarization hypotheses but is not a boundary. Its translation commutator explicitly violates [G,G] subset H. This is a valid test of the indispensable hypothesis, not a source counterexample.

The conclusion matches DetAlg71-72 exactly. DetAsm213-268 performs separate coefficient and denominator transfer. The note retains that assembly, finite simultaneous auxiliary choice and all original integral/global estimates as separate obligations. No whole proof node is marked complete.
